headline: Learned and enhanced-sampling models are mapping protein conformational ensembles
label: Conformational Ensemble Modeling
summary: Machine-learned coarse-grained models and benchmarked enhanced-sampling workflows now target transferable, Boltzmann-weighted protein ensemble estimates.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the construction and validation of protein conformational ensembles beyond single structures. Transferable coarse-grained approaches recur: a machine-learned model splits the PMF into energetic and entropic parts for temperature transfer, and MOFF2 adds residue-pair and density-dependent many-body terms parameterized from reference ensembles. Ensemble-based estimation is also applied directly, with BioEmu-generated ensembles combined with short MD and Markov state models to estimate Boltzmann-weighted populations for BRAF and CDK2. A transformer autoencoder applied to temperature replica-exchange MD of the β-arrestin 1 C-terminal tail reveals state-dependent modular organization. A complementary emphasis is validation: ProMiSE provides a multi-state benchmark, and a comparison of four enhanced-sampling methods across five biological processes shows that convergence does not guarantee correct results. FastHydroMap, a residue-level dewetting predictor, is adjacent rather than central to this thread.
